s: A multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS) customer support platform serves thousands of enterprise clients. The platform must deploy more than 5,000 customized models that use the same ML framework to classify tickets, optimize inference infrastructure costs, and maintain sub-200 ms latency. The platform must operate in a multi account AWS architecture that includes separate accounts for development, staging, and production environments. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
o: Deploy each model to a dedicated Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. Provision ml.g5.xlarge instances to handle peak traffic. Use cross-account IAM roles to grant AWS accounts access to model artifacts.
Deploy models by using Amazon SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints with inference components. Enable auto scaling in a centralized production account.

Deploy models to individual Amazon SageMaker AI serverless inference endpoints. Configure auto scaling. Deploy the endpoints in separate AWS accounts for each environment. Use cross-account Amazon S3 bucket policies to share models.
Deploy models to Amazon SageMaker AI asynchronous inference endpoints. Use Amazon S3 to queue requests from multiple accounts. Use batch transform jobs to perform offline processing.
e: B is correct because SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints are designed for hosting a large number of models that use the same ML framework behind shared serving infrastructure. This is exactly the pattern for a SaaS platform with thousands of tenant-specific models. A dedicated endpoint per model would create excessive cost and management overhead. Serverless endpoints reduce instance management but do not solve the cost problem of managing thousands of separate model deployments. Asynchronous inference and batch transform are not appropriate because the requirement includes sub-200 ms latency, which requires real-time inference. AWS documentation states that multi-model endpoints are ideal for hosting many models using the same framework and can provide higher cost savings by sharing resources across models.

w.y: Thousands of models on the same framework with low latency and 'MOST cost-effectively' points to multi-model hosting. SageMaker multi-model endpoints (or inference components) share instances across models and load them on demand, with auto scaling in the production account.

o.A: 5,000 dedicated GPU endpoints is extremely expensive.
o.B: Correct: shared multi-model or inference-component hosting with auto scaling.
o.C: 5,000 serverless endpoints hit cold starts that threaten 200 ms latency and are hard to manage.
o.D: Asynchronous inference and batch transform cannot meet sub-200 ms real-time latency.
